candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Find a common denominator and rewrite fractional parts as equivalent fractions before subtracting when denominators differ.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S01, B.S01, and C.S01 have the same operation, scope, and exclusions: creating like denominators via equivalent fractions before subtraction.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite a whole number or mixed number into a subtraction-ready form, such as adding a 0-fraction part or converting an improper fractional part to a standard mixed number.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S02, B.S04, and C.S02 all cover preparatory rewriting of operands, including whole-to-whole-plus-0/d and nonstandard mixed-number normalization, distinct from denominator matching and borrowing.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract fractions that already share a denominator by subtracting numerators and keeping the common denominator, including fraction parts within mixed-number subtraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: B.S02 isolates fraction-only subtraction with like denominators as a separate skill, whereas A and C fold this operation into a broader subtract-aligned-parts skill.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract the whole-number components of mixed numbers or rewritten whole-plus-fraction forms as a separate part of the computation.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: B.S03 separates whole-part subtraction from fraction-part subtraction; A and C include whole-part subtraction inside their broader aligned-parts subtraction skill.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract fractions with like denominators and/or subtract the whole-number and fractional parts separately once the quantities are aligned.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S03 and C.S03 are direct matches. They combine like-denominator fraction subtraction and mixed-number whole/fraction-part subtraction into one broader execution skill. B splits this concept across S02 and S03 rather than representing it as a single skill.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Regroup one whole as fractional units and adjust the whole part when the fractional part of the minuend is too small to subtract.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S04, B.S05, and C.S04 all describe the same regrouping/borrowing operation in mixed-number or whole-minus-fraction subtraction.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce a fractional result to lowest terms or convert a zero-valued fraction to 0 or an integer when appropriate.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S05 and C.S05 match exactly as simplification-only skills. B does not isolate simplification because it combines simplification with final expression in S06.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Combine the computed whole and fractional parts into a single final answer in fraction, mixed-number, or integer form.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S06 and C.S06 are direct matches focused on recombining parts into final notation. B does not separate this from simplification, instead combining both in S06.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce the result to lowest terms and express it appropriately as a fraction, mixed number, or integer by combining computed whole and fractional parts.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: B.S06 merges two concepts that A and C keep separate: simplification and final recombination/expression. Because every skill_id must map exactly once, B.S06 is represented as its own combined concept rather than being split across C07 and C08.

alignment_summary: The three codebooks show strong agreement on denominator matching, operand normalization, and borrowing/regrouping. A and C are nearly identical in structure, each separating subtraction, simplification, and final composition. B differs mainly in granularity: it splits aligned subtraction into separate fraction-part and whole-part skills, and it combines simplification with final expression into one skill. All expert skill_ids were mapped exactly once, preserving these granularity differences without making consolidation decisions.
